object_description: two elongated motorway-oriented volumes with longitudinal gable roofs
design_condition: The two volumes are oriented toward the motorway while infrastructure follows the historic eastern axis, but the first-stage arrangement leaves a noise-exposed open space and a public access axis terminating in a gated service zone.

positive.statement: The carefully coordinated roof landscape contributes to fundamentally good integration into the landscape.
The separation of staff and visitor entrances is correct for distinguishing staff and goods flows.
The structural concept is sophisticated and the timber construction is sustainable.
The carefully formulated facade creates a coherent ensemble despite differing functions.
The lightweight structural concept promises relatively cost-effective implementation.
The internal organization works and is largely well organized within the two volumes.

negative.statement: If only the first stage is implemented, the structure is positioned suboptimally and creates a large noise-polluted space.
The east-west access axis ends in an infrastructure zone inaccessible to the public and closed with gates.
Dividing the program into two volumes requires many functional connections through the only partly covered intermediate space.
The arrangement of the studios and workshops in the covered space is called into question.
The concept is unspecific and more reminiscent of agricultural buildings than of the intended collection center.
The internal organization cannot be optimally solved because of the building shape and division into two volumes.
